author: HEMALI CHHAPIA AND MANJU V
description: Captain Smit Machchhar was injured during a terrorist attack and underwent surgery in a military hospital. His parents initially faced uncertainty regarding his condition while trying to reach him. After being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, Smit's father felt relieved upon visiting him. The family decided to focus on Smit's recovery instead of revisiting the traumatic event. They remain optimistic about his healing process and future homecoming.
title: Other side of Sept 30: A family waited anxiously for their son — Capt Smit Machchhar

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In 1994, Don Williams paid $1.35 million for 1.137 acres near Maui’s Maʻalaea Harbor. More than three decades later, Hawaiʻi’s Intermediate Court of Appeals vacated a Circuit Court judgment awarding $7 million in his long-running eminent-domain case. The appellate court found competing valuation evidence created factual disputes requiring further proceedings over just compensation.
title: Maui $1.35M lot fight: $7M judgment vacated after 32 years

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Nathan Gael Montelongo, a seventh-grader from La Joya, Texas, created a project using chitosan. He collected discarded shellfish shells to produce chitosan powder and tested its effectiveness on polluted water. Studies showed that chitosan improved water clarity and benefited zebrafish embryos in experiments. Nathan designed a prototype raft that could automate water quality monitoring and treatment.
title: Meet Nathan Montelongo, seventh-grader who used shellfish waste to clean water

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In a remarkable twist of fate, a former antiques dealer purchased a painting for just $3, suspecting it held greater value. Appraisers on Antiques Roadshow estimated its worth between $20,000 and $30,000, but the auction result astonished everyone, fetching $190,000. This stunning Flemish piece, dating back to around 1650, serves as a testament to the hidden gems that can be discovered in thrift shops and donation centers.
title: Man bought Goodwill painting for $3; it later sold for $190,000

author: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY
description: Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman expressed concerns regarding the functioning of the Election Commission in India. He highlighted the issue of illegal removal of voters from electoral lists, especially in West Bengal. Nariman noted that 90 lakh voters were disenfranchised, with many not having access to justice. He emphasized the need for reform in the appointment process of election commissioners to ensure fairness.
title: Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Ex-SC judge Nariman

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Avengers: Endgame has reclaimed its position as the highest-grossing film following a re-release. The film surpassed Avatar's total box office earnings by a narrow margin after its Encore re-release. Despite a drop to seventh place domestically, additional earnings helped Endgame regain the crown. Marvel Studios expressed gratitude to fans for their support through social media messages. The success of Endgame coincides with anticipation for the upcoming film Avengers: Doomsday.
title: 'Avengers: Endgame' dethrones 'Avatar' as highest-grossing film of all time

author: NIRMALA SITHARAMAN
title: Next-generation GST aimed at boosting India's next phase of growth

author: RAJIV G
title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar faces fresh Kerala vigilance probe in 2006 case

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: The resurgence of corn buntings and various wildlife species showcases the power of collaborative conservation work initiated by local farmers. Through the Martin Down and Allenford Farmer Clusters, projects were implemented to improve habitats throughout their farms. This endeavor has led to impressive increases in populations of butterflies and grey partridges over the past ten years. Continued financial investment and diligent monitoring are essential to uphold these successful biodiversity initiatives.
title: UK farmers’ habitat work lifts corn buntings 346% and butterflies 183%

author: TNN
description: Farmer organisations represented by Samyukta Kisan Morcha rejected the government's announced minimum support prices for Rabi crops. They described the small increase for wheat as an insult rather than acceptable compensation. SKM called for a revision of MSPs and urged states to offer bonuses to farmers. Additionally, they highlighted the impact of rising diesel and input costs on farming.
title: 25p/kg wheat MSP hike an 'insult': Samyukta Kisan Morcha

author: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY
description: The Supreme Court has indicated consequences for parents of a man who abducted his daughter to the US. This decision came during a case regarding child custody between NRI couples. The father has been ordered to return to India with the child within four weeks. If he fails to comply, his parents will face legal consequences. The court emphasizes the importance of the child's connection with her mother.
title: 'Look Out Circular' against parents of man who secretly took away child to US

author: SACHIN PARASHAR
description: S Jaishankar stated that India aims to mediate in the Russia-Ukraine conflict through dialogue and diplomacy. India has recently proposed ideas addressing issues like grain and energy exports to both nations. Jaishankar emphasized America's changing global position and the implications of China's rise on international relations. India is also facing domestic repercussions due to the ongoing conflict, including commercial shipping disruptions.
title: EAM Jaishankar says US has chosen to become 'lonelier power'

author: ANUJA JAISWAL
description: In Ukraine's Sumy region, six Russian drones attacked the Kusum Group's pharmaceutical plant, killing one engineer and injuring others. The main structure of the facility was largely destroyed during the targeted strike, which occurs amid a pattern of similar attacks. The company estimates damage from this incident could exceed $50 million, impacting operations significantly.
title: 1 dead as Russian drones hit desi pharma plant in Ukraine

author: SIDHARTHA
description: GST Council plans to unveil substantial reforms aimed at improving business processes and facilitating growth. The proposed changes involve streamlined registration, easier refunds, and a more efficient input tax credit system. Decriminalisation measures are also proposed to alleviate issues for businesses with minor offenses. A focus is on reducing discretionary practices and using technology to minimize litigation. These reforms seek to enhance operational efficiency for both small and large enterprises.
title: Faster registration, easier refunds: Reform rollout with GST 2.0

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: The United States has withdrawn all bombers from RAF Fairford following an investigation into a suspected terror plot. The withdrawal occurred shortly after several people were arrested in connection with the alleged attack plans. British authorities indicated potential Iranian involvement, while Tehran firmly denied these claims and summoned the British ambassador. Additionally, the US maintains military presence in the Middle East with several ships heading to the region.
title: US withdraws all bombers from UK's RAF Fairford after suspected terror plot

author: SANJAY KHAJURIA
description: Shahid Imran, a 36-year-old Pakistani undertrial prisoner, was found unconscious in his jail cell early Sunday. He was a resident of Sargooda district in Punjab, Pakistan. Authorities rushed him to GMCH where doctors declared him brought dead. The incident occurred at the high-security central jail in Jammu. An investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death is likely to follow.
title: Jammu and Kashmir: Pakistani prisoner dies by suicide in jail

author: NASEER GANAI
description: Aasima Jan works diligently in north Kashmir, focusing on menstrual health awareness to help girls stay in school. She began her efforts after witnessing the stigma around menstruation affecting attendance rates among female students. Monthly sessions in villages educate families about menstrual hygiene and encourage open discussion about the topic. Aasima also distributes sanitary pads, highlighting their importance for health and hygiene.
title: Kashmiri teacher fights period stigma, one village at a time

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Ankith Burki, a seventh-grader from BASIS Independent Silicon Valley, created an atmospheric water generator for his project. He utilized low-frequency sound waves to improve the efficiency of water collection. Testing revealed a 117 percent increase in water production under specific sound conditions. His work earned him a finalist position in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.
title: Meet Ankith Burki, seventh-grader who boosted water-from-air output by 117%

author: NAOMI CANTON
description: Two 17-year-old teenagers were sentenced to 10 years for an arson attack at Indian Aroma. The incident occurred on August 22, 2025, when they threatened diners with weapons. Their actions led to severe burns for multiple victims, including a couple who suffered life-threatening injuries. The court emphasized the planning and intent behind the attack, which resulted in serious harm. The motive for this violent act remains unknown.
title: UK: 2 teenagers jailed for 10 years for arson at Indian restaurant in London

author: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA
description: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan condemned the extensive deletion of voter names from electoral rolls due to the special intensive revision process. He emphasized that such actions undermine the core principles of the Indian Constitution and disenfranchise millions of citizens. Bhuyan highlighted that the right to vote is essential for free and fair elections in India. He urged that no citizen should be denied the right to vote without due process.
title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan

author: DIPAWALI MITRA AND ROHIT KHANNA
description: Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced plans to implement the Uniform Civil Code. This initiative follows similar efforts in Uttarakhand and Gujarat, which recently received presidential assent. A committee led by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai is drafting the proposed laws, with public hearings scheduled across five divisions. The committee aims to gather feedback from the public and rights bodies on the matter.
title: West Bengal: Laws in 6 months to end ‘land jihad’, ‘love jihad’, says CM Suvendu

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Bailey Quinn Frank has created a groundbreaking air sampler designed to enhance health surveillance in rural areas. Utilizing basic materials such as fans and filters, this device collects airborne bacterial DNA. Findings revealed notable variations in bacterial composition between indoor and outdoor spaces. As a finalist in the Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge, Bailey exemplifies the use of practical tools in tackling public health issues.
title: Meet Bailey Quinn Frank, eighth-grader who built low-cost bacterial air sampler

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid shares more about Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes ahead of facing the Las Vegas Raiders.
title: Andy Reid reveals what makes Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes different

author: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
description: Messi moved to Barcelona as a teenager. While Spain tried to convince him to play for them, Argentina had limited knowledge of the youngster from Rosario.
title: Lionel Messi's long road from 'outsider' to Argentina’s undisputed leader

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Jon Bon Jovi’s Soul Foundation backed a housing project at the former Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Washington, DC. The development opened in 2019 with 77 permanent supportive housing units for formerly homeless veterans. The project was part of a wider redevelopment of the former 66-acre military medical centre.
title: Jon Bon Jovi foundation helped create homes for 77 formerly homeless US veterans

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: During a house clearance in London in 2023, a remarkable discovery was made: rare desktop computers from 1972, namely the Q1 and Q1 Lite models. Their significance in computing history cannot be overstated. After being displayed at Kingston University, these computers were auctioned off, with the Q1 selling for a striking £37,179 and the Q1 Lite for £8,316, marking a new chapter in their valuation journey.
title: Two rare 1972 Q1 microcomputers found in London clearance; one sold for £37,179

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: More than 300 objections have been filed against plans to convert Maidstone’s former Grange Moor Hotel into 42 studio apartments for an estimated 65 people. Residents say they are concerned the development could increase pressure on parking, local infrastructure and the neighbourhood, with some describing themselves as “devastated” and saying they would not have bought their homes.
title: Over 300 objections filed against plan to turn former UK hotel into 42 studios

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised the inspiring performances of Indian athletes at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, where India clinched a remarkable total of 85 medals, including 21 golds, finishing fourth overall. The Games were highlighted by record-breaking efforts, particularly in athletics, showcasing the talent of emerging athletes. Modi called for enhanced focus on grassroots sports development to empower future generations.
title: Asian Games: PM Modi congratulates Team India, hails ‘passion and sporting spirit’

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Rishabh Pant's birthday happened to coincide with a remarkable comeback as the Rest of India triumphed over Jammu and Kashmir in the Irani Cup. Despite falling behind initially, the team rallied to secure a 167-run victory. Although Pant missed the action due to illness, he joined in the post-match festivities. Mukesh Kumar's exceptional bowling and young talent Ravichandran Smaran's innings were pivotal.
title: ‘Thanks for the gift’: Pant’s 29th birthday made special as RoI reclaim Irani Cup

author: SUBHADRA SRIVASTAVA
title: Zelenskyy claims Putin shared jet-drone technology with North Korea

author: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA
title: Trump-linked drone firm’s Pakistan deal raises questions over US arms thaw

author: ROHITASHWA RANJAN
title: 'More involved': EAM confirms India has 'gone beyond advocacy' to end Ukraine war

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Patrick Mahomes encountered substantial hurdles while recovering from a serious knee injury, deeply affecting his family dynamics. During his prolonged rehabilitation, his wife Brittany stepped up, managing increased household duties. With three kids, Mahomes expressed the difficulty of missing family moments, which fueled his determination to overcome the challenges, showcasing their united and resilient family journey as he prepares to return to football.
title: Patrick Mahomes’ ACL rehab tests Brittany Mahomes and family

author: etimes.in
description: Mohsin Khan recently shared a delightful snapshot from his wedding festivities alongside Tamanna, creating quite a stir among fans. The photo, captioned 'The Day MashaAllah,' was met with excitement. Shortly after, videos of the couple enjoying a dance together emerged online. Following their engagement in August, Mohsin affectionately called her his 'Person,' prompting an outpouring of congratulations from admirers.
title: Yeh Rishta actor Mohsin Khan gets married to Tamanna

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: Jio Platforms is preparing for its stock market debut with an estimated issue size of $3.8 billion, which could set records. The IPO aims for a valuation of $143-146 billion, with filings expected in mid-October. Reliance Jio’s expansion includes telecom, cloud, AI, and services, reporting significant financial growth recently. Past investors include tech giants like Meta and Google, contributing substantial capital to the company.
title: Jio Platforms IPO likely by Oct-end; $3.8 bn issue, $143-146 bn company valuation: Report

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In a significant ruling, a federal judge has temporarily halted the construction of border barriers in Texas' Big Bend area. Local landowners and environmental advocates express concerns about restricted access to the Rio Grande, claiming the barriers would disrupt the ecosystem and infringe on constitutional rights. The federal government asserts that security measures necessitate these barriers. This decision has sparked six lawsuits contesting the planned border initiatives.
title: Texas court blocks border barrier construction in Big Bend amid landowner challenge

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: At a recent estate sale, a man bought a Gertrude Abercrombie painting for only $30. Upon confirming its authenticity at an exhibition, he opted to auction the piece. Titled Alderman Merriam's Shells, the painting was anticipated to sell between $150,000 and $250,000. Remarkably, it sold for a staggering $1,060,000 at Freeman's auction, setting a new high for the artist and highlighting the incredible value of art investments.
title: Michigan collector paid $30 for painting; it later sold for record $1.35 million

author: ROHITASHWA RANJAN
title: 'Equal share and equal respect': Congress's reply to Akhilesh's seat-sharing pitch

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: In 2010, Marc Benioff and Lynne Benioff contributed $100 million to build a new children's hospital at UCSF. Five years later, UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital San Francisco officially opened with 183 beds for pediatric care. Before the hospital's opening, the Benioffs donated an additional $100 million to enhance healthcare services and research. The design prioritized family-centered care, including rooms for parents and outdoor recovery spaces.
title: Marc Benioff, wife gave $100M to UCSF; 5 years later, children’s hospital opened

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: At the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, Kumkum Mohod and Sujeet Kalkal shone brightly, capturing the spotlight with their remarkable achievements. Mohod clinched three medals, including two golds, breaking South Korea's stronghold in archery. Meanwhile, Kalkal staged an impressive comeback to win gold in men's 65kg freestyle wrestling. Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha lauded their tenacity, announcing plans to celebrate their triumphs in an upcoming ceremony.
title: Asian Games: PT Usha names Kumkum Mohod, Sujeet Kalkal as Team India’s MVPs

author: SUBHADRA SRIVASTAVA
title: Watch: Russian drones hit Kyiv bridge; German chancellor arrives to sirens

author: TATHAGATA BHATTACHARJEE
description: A truck driver attacked BJP MLA Ritu Baran Sarmah outside his office in Guwahati and created chaos. The driver, believed to be intoxicated, rammed a parked vehicle belonging to party workers. Sarmah stated that the police initially handled the situation, but it escalated when the driver brandished a dagger. During the confrontation, two home guards sustained injuries while trying to intervene.
title: 'Pulled out dagger’: 'Drunk' driver attacks BJP MLA in Assam; 2 home guards injured

author: AASTHA JHA
title: 'No whataboutery can justify voter disenfranchisement': SC judge; oppn says CEC 'exposed'

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: The 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya wrapped up showcasing extraordinary athletic talent, with a staggering 54 world records shattered. While there were complaints about accommodations and transportation, the Olympic Council of Asia celebrated a nearly 20% revenue increase. With around 17,000 athletes taking part, the event demonstrated the power of sports to unite.
title: OCA cites 54 world records to declare Aichi-Nagoya Games a success despite chaos

author: SMRITI JAIN
description: International gold prices have fallen 26% from the record high of $5595 seen on January 29 this year. Indian gold prices peaked at the same time and are down around 23%. More recently, gold prices which rose to Rs 1,64,773/10 gm levels on MCX futures contract in the last week of August had fallen by more than 10% to a low Rs 1,45,991/10 gm levels last week.
title: Why are gold prices falling and will the decline continue?

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In 2012, retired FBI agent Dave Benscoter began searching for forgotten apple varieties after discovering unidentified trees in a churchgoer’s orchard. What started as curiosity became a decade-long mission. Alongside fellow apple enthusiasts, Benscoter has helped rediscover 30 once-lost varieties while preserving historic apple trees across the Pacific Northwest for future generations.
title: Retired FBI agent’s search helps rediscover 30 forgotten apple varieties

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: The McGregor City Council has reached a settlement regarding penalties related to groundwater overpumping caused by SpaceX. The city will allocate $175,000 for this resolution and commit to a 25-year groundwater monitoring program. However, residents are concerned about who will bear these costs, urging that SpaceX should take financial responsibility.
title: Texas city to pay at least $175,000 over excess groundwater pumping at SpaceX site

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: After the Asian Games, Abhinav Bindra called for a revolution in high-performance systems for Indian athletes. While acknowledging India’s notable successes, he insisted on a careful assessment of both triumphs and failures. With the Los Angeles Olympics approaching, Bindra pointed out the necessity of stable athlete growth and targeted training.
title: ‘Learn and keep moving forward’: Bindra’s message to Team India as LA 2028 beckons

author: AASTHA JHA
title: Watch: Massive fire at Saudi Aramco sites targeted in Houthi missile, drone strikes

author: AYUSH PANDEY
title: The new Israel-Syria deal: Can US solve the Golan Heights problem?

author: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
description: Kohli has confirmed that the 2027 edition will be his last ODI World Cup for India, meaning the team will have to find a replacement at No. 3, a position he has held for many years.
title: 'It’s about time': Jaffer backs left-haned batter as Kohli's replacement at No.3

author: SUBHADRA SRIVASTAVA
title: 'I do not accept': Chavan rejects Raj Thackeray’s poll boycott call amid SIR row

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: On September 30, the flydubai Flight FZ1073 faced a cockpit attack when Omani co-pilot Hammam al-Hammami stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar. The injured pilot bravely opened the cockpit door, allowing crew and passengers to subdue the co-pilot. The flight was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where al-Hammami was apprehended by authorities. Investigations have since been undertaken by several countries into al-Hammami’s background and possible extremist ties.
title: From India to Australia: How 6 countries got caught up in flydubai terror

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: Members of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) protested near Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. During the protest, AISA president Neha Bora was reportedly detained by the Delhi Police in a vehicle. Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) workers, including Saurabh Bhardwaj, were also detained while protesting at India Gate. Bhardwaj alleged mistreatment by officers during his detention, questioning the treatment of the common man.
title: ‘Beti Bachao Delhi Police Se!’: CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke on Neha Bora’s detention

author: ROHITASHWA RANJAN
title: Day 3, bigger showdown: CEC protest sparks clashes, detentions in Delhi

author: TOI WORLD DESK
title: New Jersey teacher grew 50 sheep on solar farm to 450 managing 85 acres

author: TANUJ LAKHINA
description: India's medal tally fell from 106 at the Hangzhou Asian Games to 85 at Aichi-Nagoya, but the contingent was also 25% smaller. The deeper comparison reveals a more nuanced picture: improved medals-per-athlete efficiency, an unchanged gold yield, and a striking dependence on the final two days.
title: Asiad '26: Leaner Indian contingent produces fewer golds but better return-per-medal

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
title: New lizard species found above 15,750 feet in Peru’s harsh Andes landscape

author: TOI WORLD DESK
title: Lionel Messi’s foundation helped fund €37m childhood cancer centre in Barcelona

author: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA
description: Sharmila Mona Sinha, who grew up in Kolkata, has been inducted into the National Women’s Hall of Fame. She became the second Indian woman to receive this honor, following Indra Nooyi. Sinha's journey has included time in investment banking and philanthropic efforts for women's rights. She currently serves as CEO of Equality Now, addressing issues affecting women globally.
title: Who is Sharmila Mona Sinha? The '3rd daughter' who became a US Hall of Famer

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: After studying in the US, Sharad Vivek Sagar decided to return to Bihar, despite his friends' disbelief. They teased him, challenging his choice, and he quipped that only a White House invitation would lure him back. Years later, his dedication to education earned him an invite from Barack Obama, turning a light-hearted jest into reality and representing his commitment to his home state.
title: Sharad Sagar left US to work in India; years later, White House invited him back

author: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
description: Rohit scored 92 off 85 balls, with 10 fours and three sixes, in India’s third ODI against the West Indies. India lost the third ODI after the visitors successfully chased down 352, with captain Shai Hope scoring an unbeaten 162.
title: ‘I want him to reach that mark’: Gavaskar’s special wish for Rohit before retirement

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: The Sergey Brin Family Foundation, founded by Google co-founder Sergey Brin, plays a pivotal role in advancing research for conditions of the central nervous system and energy solutions. A key achievement is the αSyn-SAA diagnostic test, which effectively identifies Parkinson’s disease pathology in living patients. With over 1,100 participants involved, the test demonstrated impressive sensitivity and specificity.
title: Sergey Brin’s Foundation backed study to detect Parkinson’s in early stages

author: KANCHAN YADAV
title: Trump announces 'Super Intelligence Force' to keep US ahead in AI race

author: KANCHAN YADAV
title: 'Russia stood by us, haven't forgotten': India's clear msg to Europe from Munich

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: During a demonstration in Delhi, police apprehended Neha Bora, the national president of AISA. The protest sought the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, but authorities had denied permission, leading to barricades that sparked tensions. As protesters attempted to break through, they insisted on being heard. This incident follows a series of protests where more than 150 demonstrators faced detention.
title: ‘Taken to unknown location’: AISA claims Neha Bora picked up by cops in unmarked car

author: VIVEK DUBEY
description: The UAE shared passenger and crew information with Israel before a FlyDubai flight whose Omani co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain and tried to seize control, AP reported. The co-pilot had reportedly been barred from flying by Oman over extremist concerns before joining FlyDubai. The incident has raised questions over Israel’s foreign-flight security system, despite previous warnings about inadequate checks and limited resources within the Transportation Ministry.
title: Did Israel ignore warnings? UAE shared info about flydubai crew & Omani co-pilot

author: SUBHADRA SRIVASTAVA
title: Moscow vows tougher strikes on Ukraine as Zelenskyy threatens Russian refineries

author: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
description: Mukesh returned figures of 6/33 to claim his 11th five-wicket haul in first-class cricket and dismantle the Jammu and Kashmir batting line-up. Akash, playing his comeback game, supported his Bengal teammate with 3/25 as J&K, chasing 279, were bowled out for 111.
title: From 89/3 to 111 all out: Mukesh, Akash trigger J&K collapse as RoI win Irani Cup

author: RAHUL.R.
description: Anju, a 24-year-old woman, has reported severe abuse by her husband Nandu and his family over dowry demands. After four months of marriage, she claims the harassment began shortly after the wedding. Anju described physical assaults involving household objects and severe psychological torment, including threats with a knife. She was brought back to Kerala after enduring this treatment and sought medical help.
title: 'Assault on her private parts, hit with cooker': Woman tortured over dowry in Saudi

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Yu Zidi, a 13-year-old swimmer from China, set multiple records and won three gold medals at the Asian Games. Puripol Boonson, a 20-year-old sprinter from Thailand, achieved a 100m-200m double with four record-breaking performances. Both athletes earned the titles of Female and Male Most Valuable Players for their remarkable achievements. Their performances established them as promising stars in Asian sports moving forward.
title: Asian Games MVPs: Meet teenage sensation Yu Zidi & sprint king Puripol Boonson

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A painting by Joseph Kleitsch that cost $100 in 1939 later gained a valuation of $500,000. The artwork depicts early Laguna Beach and showcases Kleitsch's significant contributions to California Impressionism. Following its appearance on Antiques Roadshow, the painting sold for an undisclosed amount exceeding the television valuation. It subsequently featured in exhibitions at the Irvine Museum and Laguna Art Museum in later years.
title: California family bought painting for $100; 75 years later, it was valued at $500,000

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Seychelles protected 30% of its ocean by 2020 through a debt conversion deal linked to long-term conservation. The plan safeguards 410,000 sq km of ocean, while allowing sustainable fishing, tourism and other economic activities. Leonardo DiCaprio Foundation was among the private funders supporting the financial transaction.
title: Leonardo DiCaprio’s foundation helped protect 410,000 sq km of Seychelles ocean

author: KANCHAN YADAV
description: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay condemned M K Stalin and the DMK for derogatory attacks on women. He spoke during a campaign rally in Dharapuram, highlighting the need for respectful discourse. Vijay asserted that his remarks were made as a son and brother of Tamil Nadu women. He warned of legal consequences for continued derogatory comments from DMK leaders.
title: 'Same cheap rhetoric': Vijay slams Stalin, DMK over 'vile' remarks against women

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: The Cockroach Janata Party has accused Delhi Police of refusing to register a FIR against ACP Vivek Bhagat. This refusal was allegedly attributed to an ongoing Crime Branch investigation related to the complaint. Three women journalists also claimed manhandling by police during their detention at a protest. Delhi Police confirmed the complaints had been registered and that the matter was referred to the Crime Branch.
title: ‘Doing everything to protect its ACP’: CJP claims Delhi Police refused to file FIR

author: AASTHA JHA
title: 'US a lonelier power': EAM Jaishankar takes shot at Trump's radical policies

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Following the devastation of Hurricane Harvey, Michael and Susan Dell launched the Rebuild Texas Fund, which garnered more than $100 million aimed at helping affected areas. This significant initiative enabled the reconstruction of 3,740 homes and the reopening of 1,411 businesses. Additionally, it delivered health services to 265,842 residents while emphasizing community-led recovery efforts throughout the three-year timeline.
title: Michael and Susan Dell backed $42M Hurricane Harvey recovery fund in 2017

title: Bengal to bring law against land & love jihad, implement UCC in 6 months: CM Suvendu

author: ROHITASHWA RANJAN
title: Union minister praises Rahul's Satyagraha website, then takes swipe at opposition

title: 'Not a single post': BJP attacks Congress over 'silence' on flydubai pilot Smit

author: PRISHA PATNAIK
title: Gay bar raid in Taiwan sparks protest; 51 detained under 'public morality' law

author: TRISHA TEWARI
description: For many students, entering an IIT marks the fulfilment of years of relentless preparation. But the pressure does not necessarily end with JEE. Peer comparison, branch preferences, CGPA, placements, salary expectations and the weight of the IITian tag can create a new set of anxieties, leaving even high achievers struggling with confidence, identity and belonging.
title: Cracked IIT? Now comes real test - what happens after students reach dream campus

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: Volatility looms over Indian stock markets as they navigate a complex web of local and global influences. Major factors at play include the upcoming decision on interest rates from the Reserve Bank of India, alongside the eagerly awaited corporate earnings announcements. Additionally, fluctuations in crude oil pricing and global bond yields are expected to mold market sentiment.
title: RBI rate decision, earnings, oil & more: Here's what will drive stock market this week

author: MANISHA GUPTA
description: Amid the Covid-19 lockdown, Aman Sharma transformed his unused terrace into a vibrant sanctuary for wildlife, inviting over 100 bird species and 25 butterfly varieties. With a collection of more than 500 plants that include host, flowering, and food-bearing types, Sharma aims to inspire others to create similar green spaces at home. His project underscores how urban gardens can play a crucial role in wildlife conservation efforts.
title: Delhi terrace with 500 plants now attracts 100 bird species and 25 butterflies

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Iowa livestock farmer Dave Johnson earns about $30,000 a year by leasing his land for four wind turbines. Despite voting for Donald Trump, he sees wind energy as an economic benefit, calling the steady income “the 401(k) that I never had.”
title: Iowa farmer earns about $30,000 a year from 4 wind turbines on his land

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Since 2006, Sandra Bullock has been a dedicated supporter of Warren Easton Charter High School in New Orleans. After Hurricane Katrina, she stepped up by funding scholarships and health clinics, significantly enhancing students' healthcare access and educational opportunities. In a show of commitment, she pledged to match donations for the Hall of Fame scholarship campaign in 2014, further solidifying her impactful presence in the school community.
title: Sandra Bullock helped rebuild New Orleans school, fund $700,000 student clinic

author: PAYAL DHAWAN
description: Former sarpanch Navjeet Singh Neetu was brutally gunned down by unknown assailants on Saturday evening. While driving home, his vehicle was targeted, receiving multiple rounds of gunfire, resulting in about 10 injuries that led to his death shortly after reaching the hospital. Investigators are looking into a land dispute as a potential motive, and an FIR will be filed once the victim's family's statements are collected.
title: 'Hit by nearly 10 bullets': Former sarpanch shot dead by masked bikers in Ludhiana

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: The 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya successfully ended with Qatar receiving the flag for the next event in 2030. India concluded the Games with 85 medals, including 21 gold, and finished fourth overall. China led the medal tally, securing its best performance outside its home territory. Despite organisational challenges, individual athletic performances celebrated the spirit of competition. As the Games transitioned to Doha, the focus shifted towards preparations for 2030.

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Jack Dorsey's $10 million donation contributed to OaklandUndivided, ensuring technology access for students during the pandemic. The initiative provided over 29,000 laptops and 10,000 hotspots to support remote learning in Oakland. By the end of the 2020-21 school year, access to computers and the internet increased dramatically among low-income students. The coalition later expanded its efforts to include all city residents needing digital access.
title: Jack Dorsey gave $10 mn to connect Oakland students; campaign supplied 29,000 laptops

author: TIMESOFINDIA.COM
description: Imran Khan, 73, has been in jail since 2023 after being convicted in a corruption case. He is currently held at the high-security Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi. PTI has also called for the release of Khan’s sisters and other people arrested ahead of the protest. It wants a proper medical examination of Khan’s wife, Bushra Bibi, and has demanded that their legal cases be heard without interference.

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: During the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, S Jaishankar elaborated on India's potential to rise swiftly in the global power arena within the next decade. He pointed out the country's robust growth trajectory and advantageous demographic trends. Additionally, Jaishankar contrasted the significant influence held by the United States and China with that of current middle powers, recognizing the complexity of evolving global power dynamics.
title: Where will India be 5 to 10 years from now? EAM Jaishankar answers

title: 'Will bury a dictator': Uddhav, Raj Thackeray lead Mumbai rally protest against SIR

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: Sanju Samson praised the seasoned players for their vital contributions in overcoming the challenges faced during the Asian Games final against Pakistan. India clinched victory by 19 runs, scoring 211 while Pakistan ended with 192. Samson highlighted the importance of experience in navigating weather interruptions, turning the India-Pakistan showdown into a crucial platform for their skills.
title: ‘We didn't get gold on a platter’: Samson on India’s hard-fought win over Pakistan

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Historic Randolph-Lucas-Jones House was saved from demolition by new owners who relocated it in 2013. Built in 1924 for a descendant of Thomas Jefferson, the house required significant restoration after moving. The removal involved careful dismantling of the structure to reduce weight and manage logistics effectively. Restoration efforts were extensive, demanding creative financial planning to ensure the project continued. The house honors preservation advocate Christopher M.
title: Atlanta mansion facing demolition was cut in two and moved 2 miles to save it

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: In a remarkable find during construction in Oceanside, California, fossilized remains were unearthed at a considerable depth. Expert paleontologist Joseph El Adli confirmed the identification of the bones, prompting a meticulous excavation effort. These fossils, dating back 40 to 45 million years from the Eocene Epoch, are under investigation to discern if they belong to brontotheres or amynodonts.
title: California crews uncover 40-million-year-old mammal bones 12 feet underground

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: In 1963, scientist Maurice Hilleman collected a mumps virus sample from his five-year-old daughter Jeryl Lynn. Researchers weakened the virus to develop a vaccine, which was approved in 1967. The vaccine, based on the Jeryl Lynn strain, remains in use and helped transform the fight against mumps in the US.
title: Scientist used daughter’s mumps virus to build vaccine still used today

title: No room to roam: The cost of a crowded planet for wild animals

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril, stated he is advising Project Meridian in a personal capacity. He challenged claims about Anduril being a major Pentagon contractor, asserting its lower ranking in defense revenue. Elon Musk supported Luckey's comments, noting government defense revenue is a small fraction of his companies' total earnings. Project Meridian aims to evaluate potential changes in future warfare and is linked to a Defense Secretary-led commission.
title: Elon Musk says dept of war revenue is a rounding error for his firms

author: HADI KHAN
description: In Meerut, a woman named Sunita Singh confronted her husband Mayank Singh in a moving car. Mayank was allegedly with his girlfriend, Mahi Verma, when the argument ensued. Video footage captured the dramatic moment of Sunita clinging to the car's bonnet. Police arrested both Mayank and Mahi while seizing the vehicle used in the incident. Investigations are ongoing to determine the full circumstances surrounding this confrontation and attempted harm.
title: Watch: Woman catches husband with lover, clings to car as he tries to kill her

title: ‘Utterly shameful’: Tharoor slams police action against women protesters in Delhi

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: In a shocking incident aboard a flydubai flight, the co-pilot viciously attacked the pilot with a crash axe, igniting a heroic response from passengers. Israeli individuals bravely intervened to subdue the assailant, while crew members' calls for the attackers' release sparked suspicion among those onboard. After landing in Tabuk, passengers faced psychological scars from the frightening ordeal, as investigations into the attack and crew actions continue.
title: Crew of flydubai demanded release of co-pilot after he attacked Smit, claim flyers

author: VIVEK DUBEY
title: 'Will continue to stand outside Delhi police station': CJP protests against ACP Vivek Bhagat

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: The 2026 WWE Money in the Bank is set to unfold in New Orleans, showcasing thrilling ladder matches for both men and women. Stars like Bron Breakker and CM Punk will battle it out in the Men's match, while the Women's match features talented competitors Sol Ruca and Roxanne Perez.
title: WWE Money in the Bank 2026: Full list of men's and women's ladder match participants

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Ajay Devgn-led ‘Drishyam 3 The Conclusion’ has maintained strong momentum at the box office as it enters its third day in theatres. The crime thriller opened with Rs 62 crore net in India on Day 1 and followed it with another Rs 53.50 crore on Day 2. The film has already crossed Rs 125 crore in India net and is now approaching another major domestic milestone. The immediate target is the Rs 150 crore India net mark. The franchise's established audience base, holiday release window and strong advance momentum give the film a solid foundation, but its long-term performance will ultimately depend on audience response and weekday stability.
title: 'Drishyam The Conclusion' BO Day 3: Ajay Devgn led thriller targets Rs. 150 crore

description: The suo motu case, titled "In Re: 135-Yr-Old Library 8.5 Lakh Books– And No Room In The New Central Vista Plan", was registered on October 3. The concerns centre on where the library and its vast collection would be housed if Shastri Bhawan is demolished. Reports said the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Central Public Works Department were still looking for suitable space for the library.
title: SC steps in over relocation of 135-year-old Delhi library housing 8.5 lakh books

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A broken teapot bought for £15 at a 2016 auction was identified as a rare piece made by John Bartlam in South Carolina in the 1760s. It later sold for £460,000 at auction, reaching £575,000 with the buyer’s premium, and was acquired by The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.
title: UK collector paid $15 for broken teapot; it later sold for $575,00

author: PRADEEP GUPTA
description: The political landscape in Ulhasnagar is tumultuous as the BJP and Shiv Sena alliance grapples with internal strife over nominated corporators. Allegations from the BJP highlight that the Kalani group's involvement is jeopardizing their coalition. In retaliation, Shiv Sena leaders have launched strong accusations towards Ravindra Chavan, the BJP's state president.
title: ‘Kalani DNA of crime’ vs ‘Manchekar gang member’: BJP-Sena war gets personal

author: VIVEK DUBEY
title: 'Who is safe?' Delhi minister Sirsa attacks Punjab govt after Mad Sandhu killing

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says he is very uncomfortable with people ascribing religious force to AI models, calling it a real safety issue. His X post follows a New York Times report that Anthropic co-founder Chris Olah hosted religious scholars and philosophers to shape Claude's morals and discuss AI consciousness. Microsoft and Google DeepMind voices have also pushed back, while Pope Leo XIV has dismissed machine consciousness altogether.
title: Sam Altman isn't happy that Anthropic asked religious scholars if Claude is conscious

author: ARANI BASU
description: Gill’s first year as ODI captain has exposed India’s lack of settled resources ahead of next year’s World Cup. With injuries and form issues affecting the pace attack, he wants his strongest combination finalised soon, despite a disrupted New Zealand series. Gill is also assessing No. 8 options while demanding improvement in India’s fielding and bowling discipline.
title: 'No time to experiment': Gill wants all resources available for India's ODI WC prep

title: ‘Dog-whistle politics’: Kerala CM Satheesan slams CPM over Malappuram remarks

author: CHETHAN KUMAR
description: As Anthropic develops AI models such as Claude, the focus is on instilling morals and intelligence in machines. Christopher Olah, a co-founder, raises profound questions regarding the consciousness and potential suffering of these entities. The company is crafting a 'Soul Doc' to set ethical standards for its AI, urging developers to confront their moral duties and the implications of their technological advancements.
title: Machine learning: The conscience of the creator

author: DIPAK K DASH
description: The government plans to reclaim land from the Air Force Golf Course, transferring it to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. This initiative aims to optimize the use of valuable land for community projects. Eviction notices are being served to several elite clubs, including the Delhi Race Club and Delhi Gymkhana Club, highlighting the urgent need for enhanced public infrastructure in the area.
title: Now, Centre wants Air Force Golf Course land on Delhi's Lok Kalyan Marg back

author: HADI KHAN
description: Ketan Agarwal's death on June 18 was initially thought to be accidental but later revealed to be homicide. His fiancée, Siya Goyal, and her lover, Chetan Chaudhary, allegedly plotted his murder at Lohagad Fort. They conducted extensive online searches about deaths and ways to conceal evidence before executing their plan. The investigation revealed connections to a previous death at the same location, fueling their conspiracy.
title: Siya, lover studied 'Mansi's Lohagad death', 'mushroom killing' before Ketan's murder

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: India finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games with 85 medals, including 21 golds, below its Hangzhou record of 106. Archery, hockey, cricket, boxing and wrestling delivered major successes, while athletics topped the overall medal count with 24. Tennis, badminton, esports, fencing and volleyball disappointed, while shooting, table tennis and rowing produced mixed or underwhelming returns overall.
title: From historic golf gold to tennis medal miss: India’s biggest hits & flops at Asian Games

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: India's men's cricket team triumphed at the Asian Games 2026, capturing the gold medal with a decisive 19-run win over arch-rivals Pakistan at Korakuen Stadium. With a formidable score of 211 runs, powered by standout performances from Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma, India showcased dominance. Although Pakistan's Hasan Nawaz fought valiantly with 96 runs, India's bowlers sealed the deal, underlining their title-winning prowess.
title: ‘Pakistan don’t offer much competition’: BCCI takes swipe after Asian Games final

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Bitou bush was intentionally planted along the New South Wales coast to stabilize sand dunes. This plant has since spread extensively, covering 46% of the coastline and threatening native vegetation. Infestations of bitou bush replace native plant species and alter animal habitats throughout the region. A Threat Abatement Plan has been established to manage and contain this invasive species effectively.
title: NSW planted bitou bush in 1946; decades later, it spread across 46% of coast

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Wileidy Feliciano-Rivera, a seventh-grader from Puerto Rico, transformed discarded plantain peels into biodegradable mulch. This innovative project addressed plastic waste and showcased potential agricultural benefits. EcoMusa, the resultant mulch, effectively reduced weed growth during testing while retaining moisture and lowering soil temperatures. Wileidy's work has garnered recognition as a finalist in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.
title: Meet Wileidy Feliciano-Rivera, seventh-grader whose plantain mulch cut weeds 53%

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Recent surveys have revealed six new population groups of the Mojave poppy bee, surprising biologists with the species’ extended range and resilience. Despite this positive news, a population group in Utah was unfortunately noted as lost. Findings suggest that the Mojave poppy bee does not currently warrant protection under the Endangered Species Act, but conservation efforts will persist to enhance its habitat monitoring.
title: US biologists find 6 new Mojave poppy bee groups, easing extinction concerns

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: In the first eight months of 2026, the situation in Ukraine has become increasingly dire, with civilian casualties and injuries rising sharply. Reports indicate that nearly 2,500 civilians have been impacted by missile strikes and aerial attacks, targeting both densely inhabited regions and critical infrastructure. As winter draws near, the damaging strikes on energy facilities have further jeopardized essential services, leaving civilians in a precarious state amid the continuing conflict.
title: One casualty every 23 minutes: Civilian fatalities mount as Ukraine war intensifies

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: The shop owner said that deposited cash had come from sales generated by his pharmacy and had been properly recorded for in the concerned business books. To support his explanation, he submitted an audited balance sheet, VAT (value-added tax) returns and sample sales invoices. The Assessing Officer (AO), however, did not accept his account.
title: Rs 2.47 cr cash deposit gets tax notice: Why ITAT Delhi ruled in favour of assessee

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Larry Ellison has purchased eight residential properties in Palm Meadows Estates, Florida, for his household staff. These properties, costing nearly $10 million, are located conveniently near his main estate. Residents expressed concerns over the clustering of properties under a single corporate owner, prompting new ownership restrictions by the homeowners association. The homes will accommodate domestic employees and private educators for his children.
title: Larry Ellison bought homes near his Florida mansion, quite purchase made residents upset

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: In the fourth instalment of TimesofIndia.com's series looking back at India's medal-winning campaigns at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Vantika Agrawal reflects on her women's team's bronze-medal journey. The 24-year-old discusses the setbacks against Poland and China, her individual bronze, the team's resilience, her limited exposure to elite tournaments, and her ambitions to break into the top circuit.
title: 'India's Got Latent' Gambit? Behind Vantika's double bronze at Chess Olympiad

title: 'Not afraid of death': Co-pilot's chilling admission after trying to crash flydubai jet

author: PANKUL SHARMA
description: In an unprecedented initiative, thousands of pilgrims at Kedarnath are carrying down plastic waste voluntarily. The local administration's 'Carry Me Back' campaign has facilitated the collection of over 12 tonnes of waste. Volunteers from various states, including Tamil Nadu and Odisha, are actively participating in the effort.
title: In a 1st, thousands of Kedarnath pilgrims bring back tonnes of trash from shrine

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Lewis Hamilton bought the 8,908-square-foot Penthouse H at 443 Greenwich Street for $43.99 million in 2017 but never lived there. He listed it for $57 million in 2019 before it entered contract at $49.5 million in 2021. The sale gave him a gross gain of about $5.5 million, while Jennifer Gates was later linked to the property.
title: Lewis Hamilton sells $43.9 million NYC penthouse for $49.5 million

title: US Marine arrested in Japan over murder, robbery of local woman

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: Shubman Gill has successfully equaled the impressive record of MS Dhoni, achieving seven Player of the Series awards in ODIs. This remarkable feat was accomplished following India's recent series victory against the West Indies, where Gill scored 110 runs and an incredible unbeaten 233 in the first two matches. Despite a loss in the third match, his consistent performance places him among legends like Yuvraj Singh and Sourav Ganguly.
title: Shubman Gill equals MS Dhoni, Yuvraj Singh to enter elite India club

author: AARAV DENGLA
description: For much of its history, the world chess championship was not a title a player could simply qualify to challenge for. From Steinitz–Zukertort in 1886 to the long disputes involving Lasker, Capablanca and Rubinstein, challengers had to raise money, negotiate terms and persuade champions to play. As Gukesh prepares to defend his title against Sindarov in Geneva, the USD 2.5 million match offers a striking contrast: the challenger has earned his shot through a formal qualifying system.
title: The Price of a Title Shot: When challengers had to pay to face the champion

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Scientists investigated María Branyas Morera, the world's oldest verified living person, after her 117th birthday. They collected various biological samples, revealing a mixture of extreme old age signs and youthful features. Despite her short telomeres, she showed less chronic inflammation and a healthy metabolic profile. Her gut microbiome resembled that of younger individuals, raising many fascinating questions.
title: 117-year-old woman's cells shocked scientists: Biologically much younger

author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
description: Carole King purchased Robinson Bar Ranch in Idaho in 1981 and worked on restoring the property for decades. The property, which spans 128 acres, includes various structures and natural features. After significant renovations, the ranch was listed several times before selling for $3.99 million. Its history includes being a mining claim and a resort under previous owners. The ranch exemplifies King's connection to a unique lifestyle away from urban centers.
title: Carole King's 128-acre Idaho ranch, home for 35 years, sells for $3.99M

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Carter Church, a skilled AI engineer, has managed to crack an elusive military message from 1809, originally ordered by Napoleon. The document remained indecipherable for 217 years because the cypher key was lost. By merging AI technology with historical inquiry, Church unveiled details about troop placements before the Austrian conflict.
title: Napoleon's 1809 code baffled for 217 years, AI cracked it in 6 hours

author: PRACHI KUMAWAT
description: On October 3, three female journalists reported instances of sexual harassment to the Delhi Police during a protest. These cases were referred to the Crime Branch for further inquiry. This protest, directed at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar regarding alleged electoral roll discrepancies, resulted in the detention of hundreds, raising concerns regarding the police's handling of the situation, with opposition leaders condemning the use of violence and unauthorized protest measures.
title: FIR lodged after 3 women journalists allege sexual harassment at Delhi protest

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: In a strategic move, Russia has targeted crucial bridges spanning the Dnipro River in Kyiv, severely impacting transportation and essential infrastructure. The attacks have led to significant traffic congestion throughout the city, with public transport facing notable disruptions. The Southern Bridge has experienced considerable damage, hindering metro services crucial for daily commuters. In light of these assaults, Ukrainian authorities are exploring alternative options to ensure vital crossings remain operational.
title: Bridges under attack: Why Russia is targeting Kyiv's vital crossings

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: The Walt Disney Company is preparing to restructure its extensive television operations, which may lead to layoffs. This overhaul is part of a larger initiative to streamline its corporate structure under new CEO Josh D’Amaro. As part of the changes, Disney's legal division is also expected to face job cuts. The reorganization aims to unify production teams in response to changing consumer viewing habits.
title: Disney layoffs have already hit marketing & other teams, but there may be more to come

author: VINEET RAMAKRISHNAN
description: India defended only eight of its 28 Hangzhou golds at Aichi-Nagoya, with 20 titles changing hands. All seven shooting golds and all six athletics titles were lost, but the gold medals were replaced from a wider pool. Thirteen came from events where India had won silver or bronze, or had not reached the podium. From Pranavi Urs to Lovlina Borgohain, the medal map changed even as traditional strengths remained again.
title: India’s Asian Games medal map changed: 20 Hangzhou golds gone, 13 new routes to gold

author: RAJEEV SINGH
description: "Had there been no alliance (with the Samajwadi Party), they (Congress) wouldn't have won a single seat. It even reached a point where their top leader Rahul Gandhi was ready to give up his seat. He contested from elsewhere (Raebareli) instead of Amethi. He was so scared," SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel said.
title: 'Rahul was scared to fight from Amethi in LS polls' remark by SP draws Cong's ire

author: TNN
description: A chaotic scene unfolded at a Samajwadi Party press conference in Gorakhpur when a physical clash erupted. It was reported that aspiring candidate Kamlesh Singh slapped former district president Nagina Sahni, following a seating disagreement amidst a packed venue. The atmosphere grew tense, prompting intervention from senior leaders who sought to diffuse the altercation.

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 – The Conclusion earned Rs 53.50 crore on Saturday, down 13.7% from Friday, per Sacnilk. The Abhishek Pathak thriller crossed Rs 100 crore in two days, with Rs 115.50 crore in India and Rs 177.10 crore worldwide. It is expected to pass Rs 150 crore by Sunday.
title: Drishyam 3 box office day 2: Ajay Devgn thriller races past Rs 100cr

author: PRISHA PATNAIK
description: China's foreign ministry has condemned a US congressional committee's criticism of Starbucks for opening stores in Xinjiang. The US claims genocide against the Uyghur minority in the region, which China denies vehemently. Despite the accusations, Starbucks intends to continue its business operations in Xinjiang. The company recently expanded through a joint venture in China, increasing its nationwide presence.

title: ‘Crushing democracy in their DNA’: Shivraj on Congress demanding return to ballot papers

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Lockheed Martin plans to enhance its manufacturing capabilities in India if selected for the medium transport aircraft contract. The company already collaborates with Tata Advanced Systems for C-130J component production in India. The Indian Air Force seeks 60 medium transport aircraft to modernize its fleet due to aging aircraft. Competitors in this bid include Tata, Mahindra, and Adani Defence, partnering with global manufacturers.
title: Lockheed Martin eyes bigger India footprint with $10.5bn military aircraft bid

author: PRACHI KUMAWAT
description: Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das urged Delhi Police to register an FIR against ACP Vivek Bhagat. The demands followed allegations of sexual assault against an independent journalist during protests. Protesters have gathered outside the police station, insisting on action from the police.
title: ‘Protecting a monster’: CJP sets noon deadline for FIR against Delhi ACP

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: 'We don’t do background checks on foreign pilots': Israeli minister on flydubai incident

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Earlier this year, Travis Kelce won the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Charity Challenge for the third time, earning a $35,000 donation. He directed the money to Kansas City nonprofit Operation Breakthrough instead of his own Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation. The decision came amid scrutiny of his charity’s spending, tax filings and governance. Kelce’s business manager said reporting errors are being corrected and the foundation is strengthening its oversight.
title: Travis Kelce's $35K donation draws attention amid foundation scrutiny

author: TIMESOFINDIA.COM
description: In a tragic incident in Irkutsk, Russia, a laboratory worker died after an accidental exposure to live plague bacteria from a broken test tube. Nearly 200 individuals potentially exposed to her are undergoing medical monitoring. Hospital reports revealed she exhibited severe pneumonia-like symptoms prior to her death. Fortunately, all assessed contacts have tested negative for the plague, alleviating some concern among health officials.
title: Plague in Siberia: Lab worker dies after test-tube accident; 200 contacts monitored

author: etimes.in
description: Salman Khan shared how he faced negativity surrounding his personal life and career after Maine Pyar Kiya. Upon being offered Dus Ka Dum, he was initially hesitant due to the ongoing negativity. His father advised him to be himself, which changed people's perceptions. Viewers began to connect with him as a person rather than just an actor.
title: Salman Khan reveals ‘10 Ka Dum’ helped him overcome his ‘Negative’ image

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Yemen's government has launched military strikes aimed at Houthi positions in Sanaa, marking a significant escalation amid the Houthis' recent announcement of a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia. As tensions rise, reports indicate that Saudi Arabia could unleash a major offensive against Houthi forces along the Red Sea coast, potentially mobilizing over 100,000 Yemeni troops depending on the operation's scale.
title: Yemeni govt strikes Houthis as tensions rise amid reports of planned Saudi offensive

author: NITESH DUBEY
description: Alex Albon considers Singapore and Malaysia his two Formula 1 home races, but the Williams driver wants Thailand to join that list. With Thailand targeting a potential F1 race in Bangkok from 2028, Albon’s Thai heritage could give him a third home event. Speaking to the Times of India ahead of the Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang, Albon also discussed his growing role in developing Williams’ future cars and the value of driver experience.

author: RAJEEV SINGH
description: I am very uncomfortable about people trying to ascribe religious force or a surrender of human judgment to AI models, and think it is a real safety issue," Altman said in a post to X. The comments were widely seen as a criticism of Anthropic and its co-founder Dario Amodei, who previously worked with Altman at OpenAI.
title: Sam Altman criticises Anthropic’s push to explore AI consciousness and religion

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: The cooking techniques used for potatoes can greatly influence their flavor and texture. Boiling softens the insides, while frying them post-boiling yields a delightful crispiness that has made this combination a favorite in various cuisines. However, boiling can lead to a loss of some vitamins, and while frying adds dietary fiber, it's important to note that simply combining these methods does not significantly enhance health benefits.
title: Does boiling potatoes before frying make them tastier and healthier?

author: YUDHVIR RANA
description: Mad Sandhu, a well-known LGBTQ+ influencer and make-up artist, was shot dead in Amritsar. He was attacked while collecting his car after a wash on Loharka Road. Police have indicated they possess solid leads to identify the attackers and were investigating various angles for a motive. Previously, Sandhu faced objections from a Nihang group regarding his social media content and fashion choices.
title: 'Nihangs objected to clothing': Mystery surrounds LGBTQ+ influencer's killing

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: After battling viral fever and a rushed recovery, Neeru Dhanda arrived at the Asian Games 2026 with a dream of winning a medal. She left Aichi-Nagoya with three medals - two golds and a silver - and her sights now firmly set on the Los Angeles Olympics. With the World Championship in Doha her immediate target, Neeru wants to win an Olympic medal and end India’s long wait for a shotgun medal.
title: Neeru Dhanda eyes Olympic medal to end wait since Rajyavardhan’s 2004 silver

author: AVISHEK KUMAR
description: Sambhav Jain, a 28-year-old software engineer, died by suicide after jumping from a 41st-floor balcony. He had been staying alone in an Airbnb and expressed feelings of depression before the incident. Police are investigating personal difficulties and financial issues stemming from a recent divorce and medical expenses. Jain's father had suggested he return home to resolve a monetary dispute. The authorities are examining evidence, including CCTV footage and WhatsApp messages.
title: 'Divorce, Rs 30 lakh hospital bill': What led to techie's fatal jump from Supernova

author: TNN
description: A 19-year-old BCom student named Yogesh was fatally stabbed in Nagarabhavi following a classmate's dispute. The confrontation stemmed from disparaging remarks made by Yogesh regarding a senior girl pursued by Bhuvan. After gathering a group, Bhuvan called Yogesh behind the college to confront him over these remarks. During the violent altercation, one assailant used a knife to stab Yogesh in the chest, ultimately leading to his death.
title: BCom student stabbed to death in B'luru: How 'feud' over senior girl turned fatal

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: A medical evacuation jet traveling from Bermuda to Boston has gone missing over the Atlantic Ocean. The Gulfstream G100 signaled an emergency and lost contact just moments before it vanished from radar. The US Coast Guard's search efforts have located a debris field south of Nantucket, providing critical details about the situation.
title: ‘You’re coming in blind?’ Chilling audio before medical jet carrying 6 vanished

author: G S DHANUSH
description: Around 150 individuals were detained during protests at Jantar Mantar, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Those detained included prominent figures like Prashant Bhushan and Yogendra Yadav, who continued their protest at a police station. Demonstrators voiced concerns over significant discrepancies in the electoral rolls, with allegations of mismanagement.
title: SIR protest: 150 detained near Jantar Mantar on 2nd day

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Perfectionism can be a heavy burden for children, often causing distress when their art does not align with their high standards. Understanding the line between perfectionistic striving and fears is essential for recognizing a child's emotional challenges. A parent's response to errors shapes how a child views failure and embraces imperfection.
title: Kids who keep restarting drawings may show more than perfectionism: Psychology

description: Shai Hope played a pivotal role in West Indies' remarkable success against India by scoring an unbeaten 162. His innings helped the team chase down a daunting target of 352 runs with ten balls to spare. After India's innings, bolstered by KL Rahul’s 129, Hope drew inspiration from MS Dhoni to pace his batting.
title: ‘Great man MS Dhoni’: Hope reveals advice that helped him script record chase

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the Asian Games final, but controversy followed Saim Ayub’s ‘baby cradle’ send-off to 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Former Pakistan player Kamran Akmal criticised the gesture, saying players should focus on performances rather than social media attention. India posted 211/6, while Hasan Nawaz’s 96 couldn’t prevent Pakistan’s defeat.
title: 'Doing things for social media': Ex-Pak player slams Ayub for Sooryavanshi send-off

author: TNN
description: On Saturday, a stray dog in Brij Vihar Colony carried a human foetus through the streets. Eyewitness Mahesh Yadav observed the dog dropping the foetus before trying to eat it. The foetus belonged to a woman from a rural area who had a premature delivery. Her family had buried it in a pit near a drain, which the dogs later dug up.
title: Family buries foetus near drain; stray dog digs it up, carries it through colony

author: TNN
description: Jigar Solanki, a 21-year-old finance student, left his home on a motorcycle to meet a friend. Hours later, he was discovered injured and stripped in an apartment compound. Despite being rushed to the hospital, he died shortly after arrival due to multiple injuries. Police have initiated a murder investigation against unidentified assailants and are examining CCTV footage.
title: Battered, stripped, dumped: 21-year-old finance student found dead in Ahmedabad

description: In the UK, dog owners increasingly hire private fields for their pets to enjoy safe exercise. This trend has emerged following the COVID-19 pandemic, which spurred demand for secure spaces. Farmers have transformed agricultural land into dog exercise areas benefiting both parties financially. Such fields accommodate various dogs, including those with behavioral issues or special needs. Owners appreciate the safety and freedom these private fields provide amid crowded public spaces.
title: Cambridge farmer turned £300-a-year sheep field into dog park making £400 weekly

author: AVISHEK KUMAR
description: A 45-year-old woman consumed poison and died after her family was assaulted by the girl's relatives. Her husband reported harassment by the local police outpost and inappropriate behavior by the officer in charge. They had been threatened while trying to seek help regarding their son, who had eloped with the minor. Protests erupted after her death, demanding accountability for the police’s conduct and actions.
title: UP woman consumes poison after police 'harassment' over son's elopement with teen
